title: Lingering burst source attribution and soft quota evolution - notes
content:
Summary:

Short: On 2026-02-12 we observed a multi-hour sustained increase in request traffic that manifested as repeated soft-quota throttles across multiple tenants, intermittent WAF triggering, and uneven token accounting. The initial mitigation (aggressive global soft quota cooldown) stabilized user-facing error rates but left two puzzling outcomes: (1) a repeating low-amplitude burst pattern continued for ~48 hours, and (2) attribution to a primary source was ambiguous — several client keys rotated during the window, and cached upstream proxies re-played traffic.

Impact:
- Time window: 2026-02-12 09:12 -> 2026-02-14 11:03 UTC (peak 2026-02-12 10:00-11:30)
- Affected surfaces: Hosted API (text-generation endpoints), Dedicated ingress egress counters, Token billing pipeline (delay in charge aggregation for ~6% of requests during peak)
- User-visible: 503/429 bursts for low-tier tenants (soft-throttle behavior), increased tail latency for streaming clients, a handful of customers saw quota counters jump unexpectedly after key rotation
- Severity: P2 (service degraded for some tenants, but overall platform remained up with fallbacks)

How we detected it:
- Alert chain: rate-surge detector -> automated paging to SRE oncall -> coincident spike in WAF denied_requests metric -> downstream billing pipeline anomaly alert
- Key signals used: requests_per_minute by api_key, 95p latency, WAF_rule_hits, cpu/gpu utilization on serving nodes, prefix cache hit ratio
- Early anomaly note: high ratio of very short generation calls (~<6 tokens), repeated from same IP / user-agent fingerprint

Initial mitigations applied (timeline):
- 2026-02-12 10:05 UTC: forced emergency soft-quota cooldown (lower per-key burst allowance) via quota-control plane — dropped global burst window from 30s->8s
- 2026-02-12 10:22 UTC: temporarily raised WAF safelist threshold for low-confidence signatures to avoid false positives for verified enterprise customers (manual override)
- 2026-02-12 11:00 UTC: blocked 6 IP ranges after cross-referencing with threat-intel list; some legitimate CDN edges were in those ranges — rolled back selected blocks 90m later
- 2026-02-12 13:12 UTC: applied quick KV-cache eviction to prevent stale prefix reuse across rotated keys

Root-cause hypotheses and evidence: (working list)
1) Credential exfil + automated replay: Several affected api_keys show rotation events within the same window. Correlation: high request rate immediately after rotation then sudden drop when key invalidated. But not all bursts align with rotation timestamps.
2) Upstream proxy cache replay: Some bursts originated from a small set of IPs which map to a handful of edge caches. Edge logs show repeated POSTs with identical payloads but different API keys (suggests token substitution or header rewrite).
3) Misconfigured client-side retry loop + compact-generation usage pattern: Many calls were <6 tokens, which strongly correlates with a buggy retryer that resubmitted on client-side timeouts.

Forensics notes (what we ran):
- BigQuery: SELECT count(1), api_key, client_ip, user_agent FROM request_logs WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-02-12' AND '2026-02-13' GROUP BY api_key, client_ip, user_agent ORDER BY count(1) DESC LIMIT 200; saved as bq:project:sre.burst_attrib_20260212
- Trace sampling: enabled deep sampling for keys showing >200rpm; captured spans show repeated identical prompt bodies from same trace_id prefixes
- WAF: rule IDs mostly tripped were 7382 (header replay) and 7421 (rate-anomaly regex). Rule 7382 had low confidence historically and may have been noisy
- Billing pipeline: token-aggregation lag traced to an occasional backpressure in the token-ingest worker during the peak; token counts eventually reconciled but with delayed per-key attribution

Telemetry & observability gaps (lessons):
- We lacked a fast dedup view: no on-demand dedupe of identical prompts across keys/IPs — made attribution slow
- Edge cache logs are coarse (no request body hash) — we should add a short-stable digest on ingress to help spot replays without storing full payloads
- Billing pipeline doesn't stream attribution events in real-time for rotated keys — reconciliation took hours and confused customers

Permanent fixes proposed (priority ordered):
- Add short request-body fingerprint (sha256:8) on ingress and propagate to logs + WAF flow (owner: Diego, ETA: 2026-03-05)
- Harden quota control plane: make soft-quota cooldown adaptive by key-class (PLATFORM, ENTERPRISE, SELF-SERVE) instead of global knobs (owner: Samir, ETA: 2026-03-19)
- Improve key-rotation semantics in token-ingest path: if a rotation is detected, mark incoming immediate traffic from the new key with 'rotation_provisional' flag for faster reconciliation (owner: Rina, ETA: 2026-03-12)
- WAF ruleset tuning: deconflict rule 7382 false-positive signals and add a machine-scored confidence band before escalations (owner: security, ETA: 2026-03-01)

Short-term follow-ups (action items we committed during incident):
- Implement fast dedupe query template for oncall: saved BQ query + dashboard tile (assigned to Aisha, due 2026-02-20)
- Create a one-click rollback for ip-blocks applied by oncall (infra ticket INFRA-598, owner: Samir, due 2026-02-26)
- Customer communication: CS to notify 7 customers with noisy attribution about delayed token accounting and next steps (owner: Diego, due 2026-02-18)

Runbook updates (suggested edits):
- New checklist entry 'key-rotation-impact assessment' under Quota Surge runbook: run bq query, check token-ingest lag, confirm no immediate replays from rotated keys
- Add step to throttle by client_ip fingerprint (not just api_key) for transient bursts; include safe override for enterprise customers
- Add play for quickly enabling body-fingerprint header in WAF to block replays without blocking legitimate traffic

Quick mitigation play (for future oncall):
1) Identify top-5 api_keys by RPM and check rotation events in the last 60m (bq template provided)
2) If rotation aligns, temporarily pin new key to 'rotation_provisional' bucket (reduces burst allowance by 80%)
3) If bursts continue from a small set of client_ips, apply targeted soft-ip-cooldown (do not apply global cooldown until you’ve verified edge cache mapping)
4) If WAF rule 7382 is firing on many enterprise customers, raise confidence threshold and open an immediate safelist request for impacted tenant ids

Command snippets (save these in the runbook):
- BQ top keys: bq query --use_legacy_sql=false '
  SELECT api_key, client_ip, COUNT(1) AS cnt FROM `sre.request_logs` WHERE ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 2 HOUR) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() GROUP BY api_key, client_ip ORDER BY cnt DESC LIMIT 50'
- Find recent rotations: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" "https://internal.redwood.ai/api/keys/rotations?since=2026-02-12T00:00:00Z&limit=200"
- Temporarily reduce burst: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $QC_TOKEN" -d '{"scope":"global","burst_window_seconds":8}' https://controlplane.redwood.ai/v1/quota/override

Open questions / unknowns (to investigate):
- Can edge caches rewrite api_key headers? We saw identical bodies with different api_keys. If yes, is there any pattern in CDN partners?
- Why did some enterprise customers see token counters jump post-rotation rather than during the burst? Hypothesis: delayed backpressure in token-ingest. Need to instrument per-worker queue lag histograms.
- Could client libraries be misbehaving after timeout -> retry with a fresh token? Need to audit recent client SDK releases around 2026-01->2026-02 for retry logic changes.

Customer comms sketch (for CS):
- Short: We experienced a traffic replay/retry pattern that triggered soft-quota throttles and delayed token accounting for a small set of requests. We’ve implemented mitigations and are rolling permanent fixes (body fingerprints, quota tuning). Specific customers impacted will receive tailored reconciliations.

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Keep this doc as living notes until the fingerprint pipeline code lands.
- Follow up on BQ saved view and add to oncall quicklinks.

Attachments / artifacts saved:
- bq:project:sre.burst_attrib_20260212 (raw grouping)
- trace-archive: traces/2026-02-12-burst-samples.gz (sensitive; SRE-access-only)
- slack-thread: https://slack-redwood.ai/archives/C12345/p1676100000000

Status: draft for internal review; want engineering + security signoff on the WAF tuning plan before applying changes to rule 7382.

-- end of notes --
